lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: comparing growth rates over the long run
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: comparing growth rates over the long run

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: 500 grows 4% per year. Model and value after 3 years?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 52 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
A stays ahead permanently because 52 is larger than 3.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 600(0.87)^t, with t in years. What does 0.87 represent?
choices: the number of years until the asset is worthless
the value of the asset when it was new, $600
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.87, meaning a 13% annual loss
the total value lost over the asset's life

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (2, -11) and (6, -23). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 8, 12, 16, 20. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.

items.prompt: A population of 500 grows by 8% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 114 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
A stays ahead permanently because 114 is larger than 3.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3900(0.94)^t, with t in years. What does 0.94 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $3900
the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.94, meaning a 6% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (3, -3) and (8, -28). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
